_doc: Geometry and behaviour for Snap Circuits blocks, read by tools/snap.py.

A block covers `span` posts in a row, starting at its `at` post and running in its `dir`. `snaps` are the offsets (0-based) that have a metal snap; `plus`/`minus` are offsets on a source. Offset 0 is the 'forward' end of a load: current entering at offset 0 and leaving at the last snap is forward (D10 red, M7 clockwise, W1 honks). The + mark printed on a load is offset 0.

Measured from Chris's photos of the real Beginner box (Nov 2026) and the SCB-20 manual: every 2-snap block (S1, S2, L4, D10, W1, M7) is 1x3, spanning 3 posts with a snap at each end and none in the middle. A 3-snap wire is 1x3 with a snap on all three posts. B3B is a 3x3 module (`depth` 3): its two snaps are the two corners of one edge, and the rest of the case lies to one `side` of that edge. On most boards it rides the edge: the snap row sits on the grid and the other two rows hang off it (`hangs`). snap.py check refuses parts.json if any of these facts are broken (PARTS).

Blocks only stack at a shared snap: two blocks may share one post, where both have a snap, and they leave it in different directions. They never lie on top of each other along their length (OVERLAP), and a snap never lands on another block's plastic (BODY).
measured:true means the entry was checked against the real block. A part that is still measured:false is a hypothesis; snap.py check prints a warning for every unmeasured part a build uses.
glow is the colour a light without polarity shines (L4 is a white light in a clear case).
colour is only for the drawing. Elenco says colours and styles may vary, so every page prints the block's printed ID too -- that, not the colour, is how a kid finds the part.
kit is scb20, sc100, or both (same Elenco part number in both boxes). max_volts is the highest supply a part may sit on; snap.py check fails a part that is powered by a higher-voltage battery holder.
polarity: none | colour (two colours, one each way round) | spin (spins both ways) | silent (does nothing backwards).
cells is how many AA batteries a holder takes (each 1 1/2 V). glows marks a motor that lights while it spins (M7). blades is a fan's blade count, used by the Number Lab; count the real fan.
